title: The foremost
hook: the foremost in faith will be foremost that Day, the ones brought near (56:10–11)
tomorrow: The water you drink, the fire you light

segments.voice: Yesterday, three kinds of people, and your line was three groups. Did you get to your small good thing before anyone else? Today, the third group. Day six hundred nine, the end of the week.

Picture the start of a race at a school sports day. A row of kids, toes on the line, and one of them already leaning forward before the whistle. Whatever happens at the finish, that's the one who wanted to go. Surah Al-Waqi'ah has just named the people on the right and the people on the left. Then it names a third group, and it says their name twice, like a starter calling it out over the crowd.

Verses ten and eleven. Pickthall: "And the foremost in the race, the foremost in the race: Those are they who will be brought nigh." In Arabic: was-sabiquna s-sabiqun, ula'ika l-muqarrabun. The foremost, the foremost. Commentators read the doubling two ways. The foremost here are the foremost there: those who were first to good in this life will be first on that Day. Or simply, the foremost, and what foremost they are. Who are they? Early commentators gave many answers, and they fit together: the first to believe in every prophet's time; the first to the prayer when the call is made; the first to repent; the first to do good. And their reward is a word, muqarrabun, the ones brought near. Near to God. The next verses add something surprising: a multitude of those of old, and a few of those of later times. The foremost are fewer as time goes on, which makes being one of them harder and rarer. The Qur'an asks for this kind of eagerness elsewhere too. Surah Al-Baqarah says: vie with one another in good works. Not compete to beat someone. Compete to get to the good first. And the hadith brings it down to the smallest thing. Bukhari records that the Prophet ﷺ spoke of two people who'd fallen out and stopped speaking; the better of the two, he said, is the one who greets first. So being foremost can be as small as saying salam before the other person does.
screen: `THE FOREMOST, THE FOREMOST.` · `MUQARRABUN: BROUGHT NEAR.` · `MANY OF OLD, FEW OF LATER TIMES.` · `THE BETTER ONE GREETS FIRST.`

segments.voice: The practice: be first to greet someone. Sit, and breathe. Picture the first few people you'll see after this: someone at home, a coworker, the person at the counter. Pick one. Imagine catching their eye and saying hello first, warmly, before they do. If you're Muslim, that may be as-salamu alaykum. If there's someone you've been avoiding, picture them too, and the first word you might say. The bell holds the time.
The foremost. As-sabiqun, those first to good in this life, said twice, and called the ones brought near. Today's word.

Your line: first in good. This week ran through Ar-Rahman, the balance, the refrain, the two seas, and his face, into Al-Waqi'ah's three groups and its foremost. Today, greet one person first. Day six hundred nine.

howItsDone: Muslims are encouraged to begin the greeting of salam and to hurry to the prayer and to good deeds; the foremost of these verses are often described as those who are first to good.

myth: the word 'foremost' is said twice in verse ten
was-sabiquna s-sabiqun: the foremost, the foremost.
being foremost means beating other people
Al-Baqarah says vie with one another in good works: compete to reach the good.
the hadith says the better of two estranged people waits to be greeted
the better one is the one who greets first.

fork.setup: two people have fallen out and stopped speaking. according to the hadith, which one is better?
options: the one who stays silent longest.
fork.reveal: the Prophet said the better of the two is the one who begins with the greeting.

original.note: Arabic: and the foremost, the foremost. From s-b-q, to go ahead, to win a race.

trapdoor: what you thought: the foremost are the most famous believers.
what it means: those first to good here, brought near there, and fewer as time goes on.
what a scholar hears: the doubling is read as 'foremost here, foremost there' or as emphasis; 56:13–14 says many of the earlier and few of the later; muqarrabun from q-r-b, nearness.

sources.quoted: And the foremost in the race, the foremost in the race: Those are they who will be brought nigh.

notes: Pickthall wording of 56:10–11 quoted from memory; please confirm.
